ActionTemplate.description:
An Action as a Spec schedules it: the Action without its time field.

A Spec cannot name a `ClockDomainId`, because domains are allocated at `prepare`
(SB-16, TM-13a), and every timed Action names one through its
[`AbsoluteDeadline`]. `arm` resolves the entry's `SpecTime` and substitutes it.
Without the split, `ExperimentSpec.schedule` could hold no timed Action at all,
which is the one thing it exists for.

Rule: RS-49a.

late_policy.description: What to do if the lead is short.

oneOf.description:
[`Action::UpdateParameter`] without `at`; `arm` substitutes the resolved
deadline, so a scheduled parameter change takes effect at the instant the
Spec named (RS-49a).

target.description: The resource, or the Run when absent.

ArtifactMark.description: One `mark_artifact` reaction recorded against an artifact (RS-30).

ArtifactRef.description:
Large data is always by reference: a locator, a content hash and a size, never
the bytes (RS-44, Vision §50, §51).

continuity.description:
The continuity metadata of SC-30, in SampleClock order. There is more than
one whenever the capture spans a rate change (TM-13c) or a channel-count
change (SC-30a): each ends one map and starts the next (RS-40).

id.description: The artifact's name inside its Run (SB-17).

kind.description: Its kind; a Sink Module's namespace (MA-25).

partial.description: True when it was still open at cleanup, or the Run aborted (RS-26, RS-44).

BackPressure.description: What a link does when its queue is at capacity. There is no default (SC-19).

oneOf.description:
Publishing returns [`PublishOutcome::Full`] and nothing is ever dropped.
The name is the Vision's; the policy produces back-pressure through a
refusal the producer must honour, not through a parked thread (SC-20a).
The oldest queued block is evicted (SC-20).

ChannelGap.description:
A channel that lost validity while the stream continued (SC-31a).

Vision §28 requires a capture to describe a multi-channel alignment failure, and
a hole between two segments alone is indistinguishable from a channel that was
never enabled over that interval.

cause.description:
`Alignment` when the block that dropped the channel carried `ALIGNMENT`,
`Stream` otherwise (SC-31a).

local.description: Node-local ordinal, allocated by the owning registry.

CoercionPolicy.description: What to do when a Provider coerces a requested value (SB-45, SB-46).

ComponentDescriptor.description: What a Processor or Reactor declares about itself (MA-36).

id.description: The component's name inside its document (SB-1).

kind.description: Whether it transforms samples or reacts to them (MA-36).

requires.description: What it requires of its Executor (MA-36).

ComponentImpl.description:
How a component's code is identified. The Kernel never inspects `impl` beyond
its identity (MA-21).

hash.description: Its content hash, which the Manifest records (RS-45, MA-37).

kind.description: The implementation kind; the Executor's `impl_kinds` must list it (MA-39).

ComponentKind.description: What kind of component this is (MA-36).

oneOf.description: Reacts to samples by emitting Actions (MA-14a, Vision §19).

ComponentRequires.description:
What a component requires of its Executor. Requirements only: the placement
lives in the BindingProfile (MA-36, SB-25, re-review R21).

memory_bytes.description: Working memory, when it needs a declared amount (MA-36).

budget.description:
The processing budget. A descriptor never carries an `AbsoluteDeadline`:
they are distinct types (TM-15) and distinct schema definitions (MA-37).

parallelism.description: How many instances may run in parallel (MA-36).

preferred_batch.description: A hint at the block size the component prefers (MA-36).

stateful.description: Whether it carries state across blocks (MA-36).

Constraint.description:
What a Spec requires of a key. Its value is a scalar: a constraint over a list
or a map is refused, because the matcher would then need the Vocabulary's
semantics to compare them.

Rule: SB-5, decision B1.

oneOf.description: Within these bounds, either of which may be absent.
The key is declared at all.

ContentHash.description:
`sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`. The algorithm is named in the value so a later
algorithm is an additive change (OV-14).

ContinuityMap.description:
What a stream carried, per SampleClock. There is one map per SampleClock: a
block in another domain ends the map, and the Sink starts a new builder (SC-30).

channels.description: The channel count, constant for the map (SC-30a).

end.description: Just past the last sample the map accounts for (SC-30).

first.description: First sample the map accounts for (SC-30).

valid.description: Per channel, the runs of valid samples (SC-14, SC-30).

DataContractId.description:
A namespaced contract id matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$`,
for example `ezsdr.stream.cf32`.

Rule: SC-2.

Duration.description:
An elapsed time: integer ticks in a named clock domain (TM-1, TM-4 decision T4).

The domain tag is what stops 1 000 ticks at 20 Msps being added to a 200 MHz
point as a silent factor-of-ten error.

EventKind.description:
What kind of event this is. Dotted segments; the Kernel owns the five of RS-28
and every other kind belongs to the Vocabulary or Module that emits it.

Rule: RS-27.

Gap.description: An interval of missing samples in the stream (SC-30, Vision §28).

link_dropped.description:
How many blocks the link discarded inside the same interval. A block count,
not a sample count: the samples the link lost are `len − lost`, and are
unrecoverable when `lost` is absent. That is a real limit of what a dropped
header can tell us, not an omission (SC-20b, SC-31).

lost.description: What the stream reported losing, when known (SC-13).

GapCause.description:
What the **stream** lost. A closed, derived set (SC-31, decision S16).

What the **link** lost is the separate `link_dropped` count, not a cause, so a
device overflow inside an interval that also lost a block to the link is still
reported as `OverflowRestart` with its sample count, beside a link-drop count of
one. Collapsing the two into a single cause loses the device's own diagnosis.

oneOf.description: `RESTARTED`: a stream restart, as a UHD overflow produces (SC-31, OV-23a).
A per-channel break on a block carrying `ALIGNMENT` (SC-31a).
A jump with no gap flag on a lossy path (SC-31).

`GAP_BEFORE` with `lost` less than the jump on a lossy path and no carry to
explain the difference (SC-31).

stream_lost.description: What the stream itself reported losing.

Ident.description:
A name inside one document, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.

Names are compared as bytes; there is no case folding and no Unicode
normalisation, so the canonical form of OV-15 stays byte-comparable.

Rule: SB-1.

Key.description:
A `<vocabulary prefix><path>` or `ext.<module-id>.<path>` key.

The Kernel checks the prefix and the value's shape against the [`KeyDecl`] and
never interprets the meaning (audit Finding 7).

Rule: SB-2, MA-34.

LatePolicy.description: What to do about a burst whose lead is short (SC-27, Vision §22).

oneOf.description:
Legal only for a burst whose target is statically known; `validate()`
rejects it on a runtime-decided burst (SC-27).
Transmit as soon as possible and flag it (SC-27).
Drop the burst and flag it (SC-27).

LinkReq.description:
A link the Spec's graph declares. Both `policy` and `capacity` are mandatory:
SC-19 forbids a default, and SC-21's Sink rule is a statement about the policy.

Rule: SB-15.

Namespace.description:
A dotted sequence of [`Ident`]s owned by a Vocabulary or a Module,
matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*$`.

Rule: SB-1.

NodeId.description:
A node in the (future) multi-host deployment. `LOCAL` is the only legal value in v4.0.

Rule: X7 (`00-overview.md`); it qualifies every id of TM-11, SC-6, SB-3 and MA-19.

OutputReq.description:
An artifact the Run must produce. A capture whose source has no placed Sink is
refused at `validate()`.

Rule: SB-17.

feed.description:
The link that carries the samples to the bound Sink. The output is the
declaration of that link, so SC-19's mandatory policy and capacity live
here rather than in `graph.links` (SB-17).

id.description: The artifact's name inside this document.

kind.description: The artifact kind; a Sink Module's namespace.

params.description: Sink parameters, uninterpreted by the Kernel.

ParamDecl.description: One declared parameter of a component (MA-36).

schema.description: Its schema, opaque to the Kernel (MA-36).

update_class.description: How it may be changed (MA-24, RS-52).

Port.description:
A name, a direction and a contract id, and nothing more. Per-port parameters
the Kernel does not interpret — a tensor shape, a maximum PDU length — live in
the `ComponentDescriptor`'s parameters (MA-36), not here.

Rule: SC-1.

direction.description: Whether the component consumes or produces here (SC-1).

name.description: Port name, unique within its component (MA-37).

PortDirection.description: Which way samples flow through a [`Port`] (SC-1).

PortRef.description: Names one port of one component instance (SC-1).

port.description: The port name on that component (SC-1).

Reaction.description:
One of exactly four reactions. It is a table: there is no expression language
and no rules engine, and logic that needs conditions belongs in a Reactor or in
client orchestration.

Rule: RS-26.

oneOf.description: Record the kind and time against every artifact open at that moment (RS-30).

RelativeBudget.description:
A processing budget measured from a work item's arrival, in `host.monotonic`.

Distinct from [`AbsoluteDeadline`] with no common supertype: the checks that
consume them differ (Vision §19, decision T5).

Rule: TM-15.

Requirements.description:
The Vocabulary majors this Spec's keys belong to. It is the only content of
`requirements`; per-resource requirements live in `resources[].requires`, which
is the division that makes SB-2's prefix check possible.

Rule: SB-11.

vocabularies.description: One entry per Vocabulary the Spec's keys draw on (SB-11).

ResourceId.description:
Names a resource, or a sub-resource, inside the composite tree a Provider declares.

The path is a non-empty sequence of segments; `dev0/rx/0` names channel 0 of the
receive sub-tree of `dev0`. Vision §49 asks only for the node qualification; the
path replaces §49's flat `local` because a channel or a timekeeper must be
addressable (`00-overview.md` "Where these specs depart from the Vision").

Rule: SB-33, SB-34 (`03-spec-and-binding.md`), X7.

path.description: Slash-joined path through the composite resource tree (SB-34).

ResourceReq.description:
What a Spec requires of one resource, and nothing about how it is met.

Direction-asymmetric requests are expressed as distinct keys under the
Vocabulary's prefix — `radio.rx.channels`, `radio.tx.channels` — not as a single
count. The Kernel does not know that `rx` means anything; the flattening is what
keeps it generic while still expressing the asymmetry re-review R1 required.

Rule: SB-12, decision B2.

needs.description: Capabilities this resource needs from elsewhere (SB-36).

ScheduleEntry.description:
One scheduled Action, held as a template because the Spec cannot name a
`ClockDomainId` (RS-49a, SB-16).

action.description: The Action without its time field (RS-49a).

at.description: When, relative to the Run's start (SB-16).

Segment.description: A contiguous run of valid samples on one channel (SC-30).

SinkFeed.description:
The link that feeds a Sink: the port the samples leave from and the drop-class
policy and capacity of the link itself. One shape serves both a Spec `outputs[]`
entry and a Session profile's Sink binding, because an output *is* the
declaration of that link (SB-17, SB-22, SC-19, SC-21).

Rule: SB-17, SB-22.

capacity.description: Queue depth in blocks; mandatory and at least 1 (SC-19).

policy.description:
What happens at capacity. SC-19 forbids a default, and SC-21 restricts a
link into a Sink to the drop class, so `Block` is refused here.

port.description:
The port the samples leave from: a component's port, or a port a bound
resource declares (SB-15, MA-10).

SpecPolicies.description: The Spec's failure and coercion tables (SB-18, SB-19).

coercion.description: Per-key coercion policy; SB-45 gives the resolution order (SB-19).

failure.description:
Registered event kinds mapped to reactions; an unregistered kind is refused
at `validate()`, so a misspelling is an error rather than a silently
ineffective entry (SB-18).

SpecTime.description:
A resource name plus an offset from the Run's start, in that resource's stream
clock. A Spec cannot name a `ClockDomainId`, because domains are allocated at
`prepare` (TM-13a) and fixed at `arm` for a transmit stream (TM-13e).

Rule: SB-16, decision B4.

clock.description: The Spec resource whose stream clock the offset counts in.

SubResourceReq.description: A capability this resource needs from somewhere, possibly another instance (SB-36).

kind.description: The kind of node that can satisfy it.

TimePoint.description:
An instant: integer ticks in a named clock domain. Never floating-point seconds.

There is deliberately no `PartialOrd`: two points of different domains cannot be
compared at all, and `a < b` silently answering `false` is the bug class this
model exists to prevent (decision T3).

Rule: TM-1, TM-6.

ticks.description: Tick count relative to the domain's origin; a sample index in a SampleClock (TM-10).

UpdateClass.description:
How a parameter may be changed while a Run is live (Vision §27).

Rule: MA-24, RS-52.

oneOf.description: Requires a stop and a re-plan; a sample-rate change is one (TM-13c).
Applied inside the real-time path without a block boundary.
Applied by the device at a declared instant.

anyOf.description: A signed 64-bit integer, written as an exact decimal by the canonicaliser (OV-15).

A finite float; a non-finite one is refused rather than written as `null`,
because a `Value` reaches the sealed Manifest through `prepare.effective`,
the coercion records and the action log (OV-15, X9).
A list of scalars; nesting deeper is refused (SB-4).
A map of scalars; nesting deeper is refused (SB-4).

Value.description:
A scalar, or a list or map of scalars nested at most one level.

A Spec is data, not a document tree: one level is what a structured parameter
such as a capture request needs, and more invites the schema-inside-a-schema
that Vision §9 rejects.

Rule: SB-4.

VocabularyReq.description: One Vocabulary this Spec requires, by namespace and major version (SB-11).

id.description: The Vocabulary's namespace, which is also its key prefix (SB-2).

description:
What an experiment requires: intent, portable, with nothing about placement or
environment in it.

Rule: SB-9…SB-20. Vision §8, §9, §10.

extensions.description: Namespaced opaque content, copied into the Manifest and never interpreted (SB-20).

outputs.description: The artifacts the Run must produce (SB-17).

requirements.description: The Vocabulary majors the keys belong to (SB-11).

version.description: Mandatory positive integer; Phase 1 supports exactly `{1}` (SB-10, SB-47).

title: ExperimentSpec
